name: Wolverine WVR-6R — silhouette study
notes: New independent WVR-6R silhouettes with left dorsal six-port rack and right forearm cannon. No inherited humanoid component generator. Shape review 2: remove inaccurate chest port mass, simplify shoulder launcher, keep forearm cannon smaller than whole chest. Reference iteration 3: independently traced ten-sided angular chest and forebody, sloped shoulder cowlings, tall rectangular six-port rack beside helmet, and narrow angular pilot helmet rather than bulbous cylinders. Reference iteration 4: broken-up wide shoulder shields, one clenched fist, distinctly separate cannon shroud in right arm, angular knee/thigh guards and narrower reverse-taper greaves. Fifth pass: separate armored hip section bridges chest and leg roots; individual six SRM bores remain on high asymmetric left launcher. Pass 6: individually framed six-port missile rack with physically carved 2x3 launch openings. Pass 7: hollow right-arm AC5 muzzle frame and hand with individually shaped knuckles and thumb, with no dangling fingers. Pass 8: replace rounded Wolverine torso masses with planar swept armor cowlings, bring shoulder pads closer to reference and reduce shared overlap along the shoulder seams. Shape pass 9: leaned chamfered pauldron armor, forward rectangular visor helmet and thin radio antennas, broad shouldered segmented chest. References WVR-6R FSW ink and multiple miniature viewpoints. Pass 10: replaced hollow-appearing pauldron caps with solid tapered shoulder-shell contours; split the single hexagonal chest into two swept structural breastplates. Pass 11: chamfered plate-sided WVR pauldrons with hard flat faces (not ovals) and defined projecting shin fairings at knee-to-ankle; checked against WVR-6R FSW drawing. Pass 12: replace egg-like shoulder cylinders with canted eight-sided armor shields of intentionally drawn front-facing x/y profiles, per WVR-6R FSW line art. Pass 13: vertically separate reference-accurate hip and upper torso: stretch the individually authored leg shapes to 34 grid units while translating the unmodified upper components 7 units, preventing stubby limb-to-torso appearance. Pass 14: compared WVR-6R FSW front illustration, SYZ dual pose, alternate CAD two perspectives. Shrink outer side torso blocks and cant the upper-arm plates so the torso is separated from shoulders by real geometry rather than enormous oval shoulder balls.
